notes:
Xonotic runs on the DarkPlaces engine, so rcon is Quake/DarkPlaces rcon, NOT Valve Source RCON: a connectionless UDP packet (\xff\xff\xff\xffrcon <password> <command>) sent to the server's ordinary game port, cvar "port", default 26000. There is no separate rcon port and no enable switch - rcon is off while rcon_password is empty and on once it is set (see server.cfg: "Empty means rcon is disabled"). rcon_secure 1/2 adds challenge/HMAC and requires synced clocks; rcon_restricted_password + rcon_restricted_commands give a limited admin account whose shipped default already includes kick, kickban, status and "sv_cmd unban *". The same command text works typed straight into the dedicated server's own stdin console.
PLAYER ID: Xonotic moderates by the per-session client/entity number shown as #N by status (kick help: "kick a player off the server by number or name"; sv_cmd kickban help: "<client> is the entity number or name of the player"). Names are accepted too but are colour-coded and space-bearing, so the number is what this file targets. The number is only stable for the current connection - always re-run listPlayers immediately before acting.
KICK SYNTAX IS A TRAP: the engine's Host_Kick_f only treats a number as a number when "#" is a SEPARATE token (it compares Cmd_Argv(1) to "#" and reads the number from Cmd_Argv(2)), so "kick # 3 reason" works and "kick #3 reason" falls through to a name lookup for the literal string "#3" and hits nobody. The QuakeC side (GetIndexedEntity) is the opposite and accepts "#3", "# 3" or a bare "3"; the bare number is used here for kickban because it is valid in both readings.
BAN: sv_cmd kickban <client> [<bantime>] [<masksize>] [<reason>] - bantime in seconds (g_ban_default_bantime if omitted), masksize 1-4 is the IP mask width (g_ban_default_masksize if omitted). The argument parser (GET_BAN_ARG) consumes the next token as masksize only if it parses as a non-zero number, so a reason beginning with a digit will be silently eaten as the mask width; insert an explicit masksize (e.g. sv_cmd kickban 3 3600 4 reason) if reasons may start with numbers. sv_cmd ban <address> also exists but takes an IP or IP range, not a player, so it is not recorded as the ban command. A bare "kickban" alias exists via commands.cfg; the sv_cmd form is used here because it does not depend on the alias file being loaded.
UNBAN IS DELIBERATELY OMITTED: sv_cmd unban <banid> takes the ban-list INDEX printed by sv_cmd banlist, not a player identifier, so filling it with {playerId} would delete an unrelated ban. Unban by hand: run "sv_cmd banlist", then "sv_cmd unban <index>". Bans are held in the g_banned_list cvar (optionally synced via g_ban_sync_uri), not in a ban file under the install root, so no banList is recorded.
LIST: plain "status" prints two lines per player (name line then an indented address line); "status 1" is the extended one-line-per-player layout used here - format "%s%-47s %2i %4i %2i:%02i:%02i %4i  #%-3u ^7%s" = colour code, address, %pl, ping, time, frags, #number, name. accountId captures the address:port (botclient for bots, or "hidden" when sv_status_privacy hides it from clients - rcon replies are unaffected). "sv_cmd teamstatus" is an alternative that adds team information.
MOTD is the sv_motd cvar, shown on connect; literal \n in the value becomes a line break. say broadcasts from the console as <hostname> (or sv_adminnick when set). Xonotic is not distributed on Steam, so appId is null.
